official_sources.title: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 core and unevaluated-property semantics
official_sources.finding: Draft 2020-12 defines schema dialect and vocabulary identification, URI-based identifiers and references, and unevaluatedProperties processing for instance members not successfully evaluated by adjacent applicators.
official_sources.limitation: Schema validity proves structural conformance only; it does not prove that referenced artifacts exist, that measurements are correct, or that provenance claims are true.

official_sources.title: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 validation vocabulary
official_sources.finding: The validation vocabulary defines structural assertions including type, required, enum, const, numeric bounds, dependentRequired and format behavior; format checking may be annotation-only unless assertion support is explicitly required.
official_sources.limitation: Format validation is not a network or existence check, and validators can differ in optional format-assertion support unless the implementation and test suite are pinned.

official_sources.title: W3C PROV-O entity, activity and agent relations
official_sources.finding: PROV-O models provenance through Entity, Activity and Agent concepts and relations such as generation, use, derivation and association, allowing responsibility and transformation lineage to be expressed explicitly.
official_sources.limitation: A syntactically valid provenance graph can still contain false, incomplete or circular claims unless identifiers, evidence digests and temporal constraints are verified.

official_sources.title: W3C PROV-N notation and qualified generation records
official_sources.finding: PROV-N provides a notation for entities, activities, agents and relations, including identifiers, optional generation identifiers, generating activities, times and attributes.
official_sources.limitation: Optional fields must be made mandatory by the project profile where omission would break auditability or deterministic replay.

official_sources.title: RFC 3339 Internet timestamp profile
official_sources.finding: RFC 3339 defines an Internet date-time profile representing an instant with an explicit relationship to UTC through Z or a numeric offset.
official_sources.limitation: A valid timestamp string does not prove clock synchronization, event ordering, monotonicity or trusted time provenance.

official_sources.title: RFC 3986 URI generic syntax and identifier normalization
official_sources.finding: RFC 3986 defines generic URI syntax, components, resolution and normalization considerations for resource identifiers.
official_sources.limitation: URI equivalence and dereferenceability are not guaranteed by syntax alone; immutable content identity still requires a digest and retrieval policy.

official_sources.title: JCGM VIM uncertainty-budget content
official_sources.authority: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology
official_sources.finding: The VIM notes that an uncertainty budget should include the measurement model, estimates and uncertainties of input quantities, covariances, probability-density assumptions, degrees of freedom, evaluation type and any coverage factor.
official_sources.limitation: Listing components does not validate their numerical values, distributions, correlations or applicability to the target parcel.

official_sources.title: JCGM VIM measurement-result completeness
official_sources.authority: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology
official_sources.finding: The VIM explains that a measurement result is complete only when accompanied by a statement of the uncertainty of the estimate.
official_sources.limitation: The uncertainty statement must itself be supported by a valid measurement model, traceable inputs and appropriate coverage interpretation.
